sources.title: OpenAI Codex app introduction
sources.takeaway: Skills and reusable workflows are first-class Codex app surfaces; THOS helper governance should keep skills explicit, scoped, and repeatable.

sources.title: OpenAI Codex product page
sources.takeaway: Codex is positioned for multi-agent workflows with worktrees and parallel agents, matching the need for watcher-first lane orchestration.

sources.title: OpenAI Codex GitHub releases
sources.takeaway: The official release surface shows 0.137.0 as latest stable while 0.138.0-alpha prereleases are visible; production runners should distinguish stable from prerelease signals.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol security best practices
sources.takeaway: Connector and tool boundaries should minimize scope and treat authorization, proxy behavior, and local server compromise as explicit risks.

sources.title: OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet
sources.takeaway: Status receipts should be useful for operations while avoiding sensitive raw runtime output and testing logging failure modes.

design_implications: Keep watcher/notifier helpers as explicit reusable workflow surfaces rather than ad hoc manual polling.
Separate stable Codex CLI readiness from prerelease awareness before changing runner assumptions.
Treat app wrapper stale receipts as operational log-quality gaps, not proof that sibling work failed.
Use MCP and OWASP guidance to keep connector and receipt publication boundaries tight.
Prepare x2 build work around helper acceptance tests, command-surface compatibility, and source-backed safety gates.
